text:
elaine: Quick sync — I pushed a prototype that tries conditional nsys captures in the nightly perf job. Goal: avoid storing full traces every run but still catch regressions and new hotspots. :bulb:

tom: Nice. What's the heuristic? sample rate or metric threshold?

elaine: Two-stage: lightweight runtime metric collection during the test (token/sec, p95 latency, kernel-time ratio). If a metric regresses >5% vs baseline we trigger a full nsys + perfetto capture for that commit. Otherwise we store a tiny summary.

raj: That sounds reasonable. Where are we keeping baselines? Per-model + batch-size?

elaine: Baselines stored in S3 at s3://redwood-perf/baselines/<model>/<batch>/latest.json. We compare the nightly median of the lightweight probe to that baseline.

maria: How do you implement the probe? do we run microbenchmarks or instrument the actual integration tests?

elaine: Instrument the integration trace harness we already run in CI (same config as nightly perf). Probe is a short-run (50 inferences) collecting token throughput + kernel occupancy summary (from nvtx counters). Cheap to collect.

ci-bot: Started job nightly-perf-smart-capture #1872000123 for branch=main (runner: perf-host-3).

tom: For the full capture, are we doing nsys with GPU-only or include CPU as well? Full perfetto?

elaine: nsys full with CUDA and host stacks; we also record a perfetto trace for the long timeline (1m). Basic nsys command in the job:```bash
nsys profile --sample=none -o out.ns --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include=runtime --force-overwrite --capture-report=sqlite ./run_integration.sh```
If condition hits, the job switches on capture-range=timerange and a 60s perfetto data collector.

raj: We should filter out the huge memcpy kernels (they blow up trace sizes). Can we whitelist kernels we care about? kernel-selection list?

maria: We're already using a kernel whitelist for nightly summaries (matmul, softmax, fused_gelu, layernorm). Add a size threshold: if memcpy > 30% of GPU time, capture but mark as noisy.

elaine: Good call. Also compress traces with zstd and strip symbol tables after capture to save space. Storing path: s3://redwood-perf/traces/<yyyy-mm-dd>/model=<m>/batch=<b>/commit=<sha>/trace.ns.zst

tom: How big are the traces after zstd? Last full capture was ~1.8GB raw, zipped -> ~220MB with zstd -22 and strip.

ci-bot: Job nightly-perf-smart-capture #1872000123: lightweight probe completed, metrics: throughput=142 tok/s (-6.2% vs baseline), p95=310ms (+4%), kernel_hot_ratio=0.78 (+0.5%). Decision: trigger_full_capture=true

elaine: That decision looks right — throughput drop >5%. Job will upload raw artifacts to S3 and queue a diff run.

raj: For diff dashboard: are we running automatic diffing of kernel timelines? I want an automated summary that highlights new top-5 kernels and any shift in cumulative GPU time.

maria: The harvester already computes kernel aggregates per-trace and stores a CSV. We need a small app that computes deltas vs baseline CSV and renders a minimal html diff. I can wire it up to our existing perf-diff service.

elaine: Proposal for PR gating: if a PR job triggers a full capture and shows regression >8% we fail the PR check and attach the diff link. For main branch nightlies we always keep traces.

tom: We should also avoid capturing for low-impact model variants (tiny). Add a whitelist per-repo config: .perf-ci.yml with keys: capture: always|smart|never and size_thresholds. Example:```yaml
model_defaults:
  tiny:
    capture: never
  production:
    capture: smart
thresholds:
  throughput_drop_pct: 5
  pr_failure_pct: 8
```

maria: Retention: keep full traces for 30 days, gzipped summaries for 90 days, baselines forever (but versioned). Need to update cost estimate.

elaine: One more risk: NVTX capture windows need sync with runtime NVTX scopes. We had a case where a vendor kernel ran outside NVTX so we missed its hot loop. We'll add a small runtime assert to verify NVTX markers are firing; if missing, fallback to time-range capture.

raj: Sounds solid. For implementation I can add the probe collector + decision step to the existing GitLab runner script. I can send a draft pipeline snippet later.

ci-bot: Completed job nightly-perf-smart-capture #1872000123: uploaded 1 full trace (220MB zst) to s3://redwood-perf/traces/2026-03-18/model=prod/batch=8/commit=6e3f2a/trace.ns.zst and summary at s3://redwood-perf/summaries/2026-03-18/prod_batch8_6e3f2a.csv

elaine: Thanks team. Next steps: raj -> prototype in runner, maria -> perf-diff wiring, tom -> update .perf-ci.yml docs. We'll iterate on thresholds after a week of data. :rocket:
